targets.authors: Trevor, C., Gerhart, B., & Boudreau, J.
targets.title: Voluntary turnover and job performance: Curvilinearity and the moderating influences of salary growth and promotions.
targets.evidence_quote: Because Trevor et al.’s discovery is at odds with prevailing meta-analytic evidence and may not generalize to companies employing more common pay-for-performance schemes, replication of their pronounced U-shaped curve is essential.
targets.outcome_quote: Moreover, our promotion effects qualify and extend Trevor et al.’s (1997) results. Unlike their U.S. findings, the present study revealed that promotion progress did not act as a productivity signal in Switzerland. Rather, promotions deterred departures among Swiss citizens, which fits their (masculine) esteem for advancement (Hofstede, 2001).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Curvilinearity agrees; promotion effects and salary-growth moderation explicitly differ. No overall whole-replication verdict overrides these comparisons.

reasoning: New Swiss-bank employee sample re-tests Trevor et al. (1997). Other cited evidence motivates the study rather than defining additional targets.
